#3969. GTA 6 Vintage Vice City Pack Now Available To All Players On Xbox, And It's Pretty Cheap

"Flash back to when the neon burned brightest"

Ahead of the release of GTA 6, there were three types of content made available for it - the standard game, the Ultimate Edition content, and the Vintage Vice City Pack. The latter was intended as a pre-order bonus across Xbox and PS5.

Now that the game is out in the wild though, Rockstar Games has decided to make the Vintage Vice City Pack available to purchase on the Xbox Store, carrying a price tag of £4.49 / $4.99. That's obviously not as good as getting it for free, but it's pretty cheap all the same, and a nice option to have if you missed out on the pre-order period.

Similar to the Ultimate Edition content that you can also buy separately for £20.00 / $20.00, these items are made available "as [the] story progresses", so you don't necessarily get it all at the beginning of the campaign.

I have to admit that I haven't really engaged with the Ultimate Edition stuff all that much yet, although it's certainly a nice bonus to get extra vehicles, liveries and outfits. The game is more than stacked enough that you don't need to buy anything more than the standard edition, but the option is there if you want the most content possible.

We'll leave a poll down below to find out which version you personally have, and let us know in the comments if you think the Vintage Vice City Pack and/or the Ultimate Edition content is worth buying on top of GTA 6 itself!

#3968. Forage and fight for ingredients in a magical 1960s Italy and whip up some tasty meals Cooking Mama style in The Snackbar at the End of the World

If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.

First up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.

The other line reads, "Every sound effect, musical note, design decision, and line of code is human-made. Because this game is about human relationships and delicious food – and that’s not a story we would ever trust AI to tell." Thank the lord! Right now there's no release date attached to The Snackbar at the End of the World, unsurprising given it was only announced this week. But while we all wait for a date, you could perhaps join me in throwing it a wishlist on Steam.

#3967. "We Saw Your Hopeful Requests" - Fabraz Announces Demon Tides Switch 2 Release

Launching January 2027 alongside the Switch version

Critically-acclaimed developer Fabraz has announced it will be releasing its 3D platformer Demon Tides for the Switch on 21st January 2027.

As part of this news, it's also been revealed Demon Tides is launching for the Switch 2 (and PlayStation 5) on the same date! These versions of the game are done in partnership with PM Studios and will get the physical treatment at some point "later" next year.

"Demon Tides will launch on the Switch, Switch 2 and PS5 on January 21st 2027! Demon Tides had a critically acclaimed PC launch with a 95% Overwhelmingly Positive rating on Steam, 84 on metacritic and 86 on opencritic."

Fangamer's physical version of Demon Turf + Demon Tides will also be going into production "soon", with pre-orders for this scheduled to go live in early 2027. This version will also come bundled with Neon Splash.

Fabraz has also confirmed the Switch 1 version of the game will feature an option to uncap the frame rate, meaning you play the Switch 1 version in 60fps on Switch 2.

As for how each version of the game performs on its respective system, you can expect 30fps at 720p/1080p (docked and handheld) on Switch. And on Switch 2, the game runs at 60fps in performance mode, 30fps in quality mode, and displays at a 1080p resolution.

In some other news, Fabraz recently rolled out a patch for Atari's revival of Bubsy, bumping his 4D outing up to Version 1.2.1.

#3966. The Sunday Papers

The Sunday Papers is our weekly roundup of great writing about (mostly) videogames from across the web.

While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?

As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll. It growls and wriggles like a panicking caterpillar, scooting away under a table. Before you lose sight of it, you discern the title and subject of the text – it's an essay by Kyle Tam about the yokai of Promise Mascot Agency.

Deep in a drawer, you discover a sour-smelling binder full of extracts from an ancient and all but indecipherable dispute over the discovery of "generative AI" in something called "Big Walk". The stakes are long-buried, but many of the individual pieces of writing are lively. Here is Bruno Dias noting in passing that "one of the harms of the 'AI' political project is the propaganda machine dedicated to making you feel stupid and helpless." Here is a professorial interjection from Brendan Keogh calling on the warring parties to recognise when "critiques of generative AI are actually just deflected critiques of the capitalist relations of technology and labour". Here is Mike Cook arguing that "what's happening is not unusual, it's not extreme, it's not unfair and it's not a 'public flogging'." Here is a ticker tape message from Hannah Nicklin observing that "if your radical position doesn’t have room for transformation it will not be safe until it contains just you".

A footnote in the same dusty sheaf of papers points you towards another work from Mike Cook in a different drawer. This one consists of neon slides, slotted into an antique View-Master, and explores a comparison between procedural generation and street photography.

Peering at the weirdly white and opaque windowpanes, you realise there are intricate equations traced in the condensation. It appears to be a post-mortem for a "post-cosy" game called Danchi Days, in which developer Melos Han-Tani discusses wishlist conversion rates and the problem of not fitting neatly into any recognisable genre.

A snowglobe stands on a mantelpiece, the flakes still orbiting a miniature washtub as though the object had been recently shaken, even though the chamber has clearly been abandoned for decades. You put it to your ear, anticipating the faint jingle of Xmas bells. Instead, you are almost deafened by a screeching guitar chord. Here is Erin Keane to explain.

Next to the snowglobe on the mantelpiece, there's a souvenir shop conch shell, polished to a high sheen. You put that to your ear, hoping to catch the soothing shuffle of surf on shingle, and a disembodied voice tells you to piss off. Tim Sniffen has some thoughts about gentrification, and why only he should be allowed to do it.

Again, one of these mystic artefacts hides the key to your release from the suffocating stillness of Sunday Afternoon. Which will you choose? Or have you, perhaps, brought a sorcerous teleportation device of your own? Please share. Here is Joanna Newsom's Cosmia to help you think.

#3965. Digital Foundry Analyses Whether GTA 6 Could Benefit From 40FPS On Xbox Series X

"A 40fps mode with VRR could still make sense"

Over the weekend, there was a whole lot of buzz amongst the GTA 6 community about a Quick Resume glitch that unlocks the game's frame rate on Xbox Series X and S, potentially allowing it to reach 60FPS and higher.

Follow-up tests showed that the results were averaging more around the 30-35FPS range consistently, and some of the game's animations appeared to be running at double speed. The experts at Digital Foundry have now weighed in on this, and they've come to pretty much the same conclusion - that it's not really a viable way to play.

Rich Leadbetter of DF found that he reached an average of 36FPS on Xbox Series X in the first hour of the game:

"Unfortunately, while the unlock glitch is academically interesting, it doesn't provide a huge improvement to responsiveness. Our capture tools show frame-rates in the 30fps to 40fps range on Series X, with Rich recording an average frame-rate of 36fps during the first hour of the game."

The sped-up gameplay is also mentioned, described as an "oddity" that "makes the game inconsistent and harder to control", although this is said to be more likely a result of the bug rather than GTA 6's code being tied to frame rate.

Nevertheless, there's one specific advantage that's brought up as part of this glitch, which is that it reduces the game's input lag. Digital Foundry's tests showed that the game provided around 170ms of lag at the 30FPS mark, while a 40FPS scene dropped it to around 120ms. However, the varied frame rates are said to provide an "unsettling" feel overall, and one that probably outweighs the smoother feel during specific 30FPS+ moments.

The outlet says that a 40FPS mode when using a VRR supported display "could still make sense" on Xbox Series X, but "the game's CPU limits remain the largest barrier against such a mode" due to occasions where GTA 6 can't even reach 30FPS as things stand, while it might also require extra work such as implementing FSR upscaling tech.

"A 40fps mode with VRR could still make sense, but it's far from an open-and-shut case to say that such a mode would be an improvement overall against the current 30fps cap. It might also require extra work, such as integrated FSR 4 on Series X in service of a higher frame-rate when GPU limited, which wouldn't be the work of a moment. Finally, it looks like a 60fps mode is fundamentally unachievable on current console hardware."

Who knows whether Rockstar Games will be able to put in the work to provide a 40FPS mode in the future, but we're going to bet they'll stick with 30FPS and simply aim for 60FPS when Xbox Project Helix and the PS6 hit the market. They've got plenty of work to do with the PC version of GTA 6, not to mention the GTA Online version of the game that's surely in the works, so pushing to hit 40FPS on current-gen consoles seems unlikely.

@AccessibleDaydream FSR 4 intentionally lowers the rendering resolution and then uses AI to reconstruct the image. This is less demanding for the GPU than rendering directly at the native resolution because there are fewer pixels to process. As a result, the GPU saves rendering time and can use those saved resources to generate more frames per second (FPS). The end result is higher FPS with the same image quality, or in some cases even slightly better image quality

As @Gabrie suggested the game seems like it is more constrained by the power of the CPU not the GPU. You can scale GPU tasks quite easily, but it's much harder to scale CPU tasks as it would basically mean lowering the complexity of the simulation (Cars, NPCs etc.) which they are unlikely to do.

When will we return to the Lord of the Rings prequel? Here's everything we know about The Rings of Power season 4

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Rings of Power season 4 has been officially confirmed by Prime Video. Following reports from earlier in 2026 that development had already started on the upcoming episodes ahead of season 3's release, Amazon Studios announced that pre-production has begun. The third season's finale sets up plenty more to come in the Lord of the Rings prequel as well.

For all you need to know about what to expect with The Rings of Power season 4, you're in the right place. We're big fans of the fantasy epic here at GamesRadar+ and have everything from exclusive insight to all the potential story details we think the show might cover next.

Now Sauron has forged the One Ring, darkness is set to spread further in Middle-earth too. So we'll be your guiding light from the coming season, covering everything from release date speculation to what cast members are returning. If that wasn't enough to tide you over until we see more, check out our guide to watching The Lord of the Rings in order too for the ultimate rewatch.

We'll be getting into spoilers for The Rings of Power season 3 below, so make sure you're up to date.

The Rings of Power season 4 has been confirmed by Prime Video. Ahead of the release of the show's finale on November 24, Amazon Studios confirmed that pre-production was underway at Shepperton Studios, where the series is filmed.

It's clear that Amazon Studios has been working to give themselves as much of a head start as possible to allow for smaller gaps between seasons.

When it was announced that development was kicking off, The Hollywood Reporter suggested filming could begin in early 2027. Based on season 3, we can get an idea about what this might mean for a potential release date.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Season 3 started filming in May 2025 before it was released in November 2026. Based on a similar schedule, if filming starts in early 2027, we could see The Rings of Power season 4 in mid-to-late 2028.

We'll keep you in the loop with any updates on the next season when we get them.

The Rings of Power season 3 saw Sauron reach the height of his powers after forging the One Ring. In episode 7, he was finally able to create the weapon that would allow him to control all of the other rings. In the season finale, he prepped for his final battle with the help of Pallando and the peoples of Rhûn.

However, before he could reach the battlefield, Gandalf was able to bring Pallando back to the light, even if he was killed in the process. The light of his return casts off Sauron's power over the people of Rhûn, who abandon the fight. Faced with just his army of Orcs against the men of Númenor and the Elves, it's not looking so promising for Sauron.

He decides to give himself up, walking over to Ar-Pharazôn and kneeling before him, allowing him to be taken prisoner by Númenor. However, we wouldn't be so sure this is the Dark Lord giving in. This is Sauron, after all, and he will definitely have a nefarious plan.

No plot details have been revealed yet, but it seems like this is where the show will pick up again. We're also likely going to get more time jumps going forward. Speaking to GamesRadar+, co-showrunner Patrick McKay said this is their current plan.

He explained: "I think from the very beginning, we aspired the show to compress the time that's in the books, but also to have significant jumps forward in time for characters to age, for kingdoms to rise or fall, and I think you know there will probably be some jumps in the future."

Based on where we are currently in the Lord of the Rings timeline, there are several potential avenues that The Rings of Power season 4 may cover. The big moment in Middle-earth's history that looks likely to be explored is the fall of Númenor.

This has been building for a while, but in Tolkien's work we know that Ar-Pharazôn captures Sauron and brings him to Númenor. This is what's implied at the end of The Rings of Power season 3.

Here, Sauron is able to manipulate the king, influencing him to make war against the Valar. This sets off a chain of cataclysmic events that ends with Númenor buried under a huge wave.

Not everyone dies, though, as Elendil and his sons Isildur and Anárion, alongside some of the other Faithful, escape the fall by traveling to Middle-earth. Here, they found Arnor and Gondor, two key locales in Lord of the Rings history.

Sauron also loses his ability to take fair form after Númenor falls, with his spirit remaining in the One Ring. It's not yet clear whether the show will follow this or make some big changes in the coming season.

The Rings of Power season 4 cast has not yet been confirmed but we can expect most of the lead roles to be back, aside from the casualties in the season finale (RIP Pallando).

There is no Rings of Power season 4 trailer yet. We expect we'll be waiting quite a while before we see one too, given that cameras have yet to roll.

With season 3, the trailer was released at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, just over three months before the show launched. We expect season 4 will follow a similar timeframe.

When Amazon Studios secured the rights from the Tolkien estate, they made the commitment to five seasons of the prequel show. The showrunners, J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay, have been very open that this remains their long-term plan as well.

Speaking to French publication Le Journal du Geek in late 2026, McKay reiterated this too. "We have a plan, we know it ends with five seasons. That's still the plan," he told them.

Of course, plans can change, and the show may end at season 4, but we would be pretty surprised if it did. This means that we should be in for two more epic seasons to conclude this story.

For more, check out our The Rings of Power season 3 review and The Rings of Power season 3 ending explained for a full breakdown.

#3963. GTA 6 Is 'Probably the Greatest Artistic Achievement in History', Says Cyberpunk 2 Director

Just about every veteran developer in the industry has been heaping praise on GTA 6 since its release last week, but I'm not sure any of that rampant positivity matches the thoughts of Igor Sarzynski.

Sarzynski is currently the creative director on Cyberpunk 2 (as it's officially known right now), having previously worked on both The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 — two games that are widely considered to be amongst the best that the open world genre has to offer.

In other words, Sarzynski knows what he's talking about when he says GTA 6 is "probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history". Now that's praise.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," he noted on social media.

"Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle."

"Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled," Sarzynski jokes, suggesting that no one's going to match Rockstar's effort for quite some time. "I'mma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now."

If you've played GTA 6, you can surely understand why every non-Rockstar developer is looking at it and being left in a state of near disbelief. We're not getting another release like it for years and years to come — and just like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it, it's going to become the benchmark for open world games.

Still, there'll come a time when Cyberpunk 2 takes all the headlines — it's just that right now, it's hard to see beyond GTA 6 because it's absolutely bloody everywhere (and with good reason).

"Seriously though I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavour," Sarzynski continues in a follow-up post.

"GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed," he concludes — and that's pretty much a perfect way to put it.

In 1501 Michaelangelo sourced a 17ft piece of marble from a quarry in Tuscany and had it moved 57km to Florence. Over the next 3 years with rudimentary hand tools he chipped away at the stone, knowing that any mistake could ruin his creation and threaten his standing with his patron Lorenzo de Medici. He succeeded and gave the world the statue of David, the first colossal marble antiquity.

Art is subjective, one’s reaction and like to it is also a subject objectively personal experience, as in no one can deny your reaction or take it away from you.

However, I get what Igor means completely. Some of the previous comments here lament over how beautiful and awe inspiring of an artistic expression numerous historical works are.

They then don’t mention if they’ve seen them in person at all or whether they’re mentioning them simply due to falling asleep to a BBC documentary.

Now I have seen some of these “greatest artworks of all time”, and no, they didn’t make me feel the way I (Igor and many others in and out of the industry) feel when looking at GTA6.

Carving something out of marble is a beautiful achievement, one that should stand the test of time as a lesson in art imitating life, the expression of the body itself.

However, that, or a bloke painting on some plaster on a ceiling hasn’t ever brought reactions to as many as certain other artworks have. They are acclaimed for so many other reasons than their achievements.

In fact, one could argue classical art serves more intrinsically important roles in generating tourism, money for locations and to prop up the historical and classical art scene.

My mother was an artist and art lecturer, and she taught me growing up that all art can evoke feelings in the right person, but that’s doesn’t mean all art is an equal achievement to all.

Personally for example, I think the arrogance and lack of expressionism for anything other than the predictable in these classic art pieces bores me. Yet that’s me, and my opinion. Subjective.

GTA6 makes me feel the way I’ve felt very few times when considering artwork of any kind, and for that, I’d agree more with Igor.

There is nothing I’m aware of in production for PS6 that I would say anyone that I work with is expecting to beat or even equal GTA6 in some of the technical achievements.

At present, from all I know of what is both completely out to the public and not, R* have set a bar. It will be raised, in part and in full. But we are not talking PS6 release raising it fully.

So far, I’d say Witcher 3’s a bigger artistic statement, but GTA6 is a FAR bigger technical achievement from what I’ve played so far. I need more time in the game to make definitive statements, but I think the game will be sort of divisive with the nerds in the long run because of how many people are saying “it’s better than everything ever, quit game development.” I mean, we literally had a similar wave with Clair Obscur last year. All the same things were said about Baldur’s Gate 3. This kind of thing sort of causes retaliation as much as celebration these days.

I'm not trying to be disrespectful here, so please understand that, but you do have to wonder what other developers could do with an £800 million budget and an allowance of 8 to 10 years to complete their game.

I'm not trying to put Rockstar down here. I have not played GTA 6 (and may not), but the truth is that most developers are given half the time that Rockstar took to make GTA 6, and also a third of the budget at most. Instead of pushing boundaries, as Rockstar have done, most developers are looking for ways to cut corners and get their games out as soon as possible.

Honestly, if a developer such as Larian or CD Red were afforded the time and the money to make the game they really wanted, I am sure we would be equally amazed at what they produce. The truth is, when you look at what Larian and CD Red achieve with a fraction of the budget and half the time, then it makes you realise what technical marvels their games turn out to be.

When you see how much money GTA 6 has made (a return of something like 8 times the amount the game cost to make) you do have to wonder whether any other developer is actually in a position to do something similar, and the answer is probably not...

@Fiendish-Beaver I don’t disagree with your statement in many ways.

However, on the subject of CDPR, with Cyberpunk 2077, every AAA and some even AA studios could absolutely deliver what they have.

They started “work” on Cyberpunk 2077 as far back as 2010-2011 if memory serves.

It was then in and out of development, until about 2016 when it was an all hands on deck approach. Not the start of development, simply at that point many more in the studio working on actively producing a working title.

Then, release came, again, I believe was around 2020. So say at that point 9-10 years of development, with 4 or just under/over years of true entire studio development of some sort.

Yet, they released a game so bad in its basic coding and functionality, that they claimed they weren’t aware of, to then claim they were aware of, then had journalists embargo to not tell of this until launch/very close to launch.

They then offered mass refunds, one of the industries first physical and digital refunds of its kind. Where even I sent them my disc back to their office directly and got a refund.

It then took them up until shall we say about now, maybe being generous a year or so ago to get the game to where most were led to believe it should be and would have been at release.

CDPR conned the public, for financial gain, knowingly, and they squandered hundreds of thousands and likely millions actually on course correcting.

When all they had to do was not release the game until it was finished.

So whilst from what I witness every day in the industry I agree with your points as a whole, we shouldn’t give credit to what CDPR could do with a billion dollars, when the best example of what they did with less was verging on fraudulently selling and advertising a product, pulling it from sale, taking years to “fix” it and then regain consumer confidence.

Many may have forgiven and/or forgotten. They shouldn’t, and I sure won’t.

CDPR have a wonderful vision in their artistry, and I hope they go on to have success upon success. But what R* have achieved is miles beyond what many could achieve even with the money.

There’s numerous engines I’ve used over the years, entire workflows that quite literally can’t physically do what R* have pulled off with their team and technology. It needs really making clear to the laypeople of the world that this isn’t simply more money and talent, this is entirely new ways of approaching how to develop a game and how to use the the resources available.

CDPR literally looked at what they had, made mockups of ideas that were conceptual at best and ran with selling concept art that in some cases they still haven’t accomplished.

I don’t even have a history of playing a lot of R* content. But they have achieved something that money can’t currently buy. That’s the impressive part.

However, as stated, completely agree and disagree but not entirely. 😂 Peace and love on earth etc.

Totally agree, @ButteredCrumpet. I really don't understand where it all went so wrong with CDPR. The game looked immense before it was released, and I bought into it, yet we had all been conned. How on Earth did they think they could get away with it?

To be fair to them, they have righted the ship, and the game is completely different now to when it first launched, and I think what CPDR did has been a lesson from which the industry has (mostly!) learned (looking at you Mindseye!), and regardless of that I think that CPDR know more than anyone that all their future releases will be met with a degree of scepticism. I do not expect Cyberpunk 2 to release in the broken state that the first game did. Maybe I've being naïve, but I would like to think they know better than to do that again...

@Fiendish-Beaver Absolutely agree. I believe in them, their talent and their capacity to deliver a game time and time again that is astounding.

Though I didn’t know of anyone on a personal level that worked on the project, it was clear early on something was not quite right with how the studio was handling things internally.

I even remember there being a time where more effort was seemingly being spent on a website, clues for the public and pre-rendered concept art than the game. As at that time they then claimed it was just a pipe dream of sorts.

Yet oddly one they were releasing next and seemingly had not even a mockup of a room or street lamp to speak of.

I personally think they got lost in the vision for a while, knowing as creatives they were onto something new and special. Almost like an artist staring at an oil painting for too long will always find a way to critique and amend it, yet not always objectively improve it.

I have now since gone back to Cyberpunk 2077 and though struggled at first to enjoy it, it has since clicked and I have had a wonderful time with it.

I think the biggest problem in development right now that I am witnessing first had, is simply too many suits trying to predict the next big thing, instead of allowing the next big thing to be naturally found.

Working in lighting and texturing, I can’t create the next big thing, I sort of have to discover it. But of course, that’s where the time and money element do apply. As without it I can’t excuse spending 6 months on a global sabbatical just meandering through the technology and discovering things on a whim.

It’s an odd industry really, it’s a lot like being a pop star, you’re told what to create, the timeline for when it’s expected to be completed, told how much will be charged for it, where and when it will be sold.

Yet you’re never really being told this by people who have much if any experience achieving it, so then you sit back and realise you may not be happy with something, but then my happiness with a texture doesn’t matter.

My happiness with the art I create matters only to the person viewing, yet the person that decides everything I create cares not for my happiness with it.

However, I’m only experiencing what many in and out of creative jobs experience. It’s not like it’s any different being told to move an Amazon parcel onto a conveyor and not wishing to.

I just sometimes wish we could all stop the conveyor and question why some things are being placed on it.

Art shouldn’t be rushed, as the historical examples people have provided on this site show, but then there is little to no industry without reliable performance, predictable results and financial investment.

In an ideal world art and money would never cross paths, but then tell that to Sotheby’s. An entire world of elitist ideals based on paintings by people who died financially bankrupt helping to prop up the wealth of the few.

Hardly what Rembrandt would have really wanted.

Thank you for your insight, @ButteredCrumpet. That was really interesting. Although not being able to paint or draw, nor hold a note or being computer literate, I do totally get what you mean about a creative starting at a canvas and seeing everything that they want to improve about the work they have done; about 25 to 30 years ago, I set about writing 3 novels. I finished two of them, and got part way through the third. The first two were in excess of 100,000 words, so these were not short stories. Problem is, I was forever going back through them and altering elements, and instead of shortening them, they would end up longer still, and I was always tinkering with them.

I often think about revisiting them as I never tried to get them published, but things changed for me when I met my second (now sadly deceased) wife. When I met her I dropped my writing, and even after her passing, I never returned to it, and instead fell headlong into gaming, and now I just cannot imagine spending long hours writing instead of gaming. Don't misunderstand me, I loved writing, and the writing process, but I think I probably enjoy gaming more, and so I'm not sure I'll return to it, but never say never, I guess...

@dark_knightmare2 It's a real shame that you're taking a celebration of what most believe is a landmark achievement in gaming and finding some way to be miserable about it. You're the guy at a baby shower talking about how the cake sucks.

@Fiendish-Beaver I am tremendously sorry to hear of the passing of your late wife that you experienced. Experiencing a great deal of loss myself, I know how much isn’t described by simply stating they are lost.

They’re there, in reverberations and memories at the very least, but grieving is a process I don’t believe fully ends, you sort of just learn to see things through another lens. Sometimes that is rose tinted and sometimes it’s darkness, but it’s always possible to see through them in time.

I won’t for a second try to tell you what to do, but maybe in time try to compel yourself to finish the writing, not in spite of all you experienced and how it changed you, but to have something you experienced change the way you write subconsciously and have it remembered forever.

When I lost my parents, I thought I’d change my career, I couldn’t create because all I could think of was the sheer volume of loss. How does one go about adding to the world when so focused on what has been taken from it.

Yet I found a way, I somehow found a way to regain a confidence not in myself, but in wanting to allow the light to win, and allow the work to speak of something I might not fully understand, but hopefully marks a time for someone out there that can gain from it.

Either way, you’re a creative with a story to tell. I for one would very much like to purchase anything literary you create no doubt.

Just remember, art knows no time, it’s there waiting for you if you ever find a moment.

I once tried to write a book on my dad’s typewriter, but then quickly learned it’s a very vulnerable process. Hence, I stopped, as vulnerability after a loss is never something one yearns for.

I think you will publish one day, the time will present itself, when it does, let me know. Who knows, it could help to heal another not just yourself.

In the meantime, gaming being your escapism only adds strings to your subconscious bow. If you ever need to scream or almost silently whisper, creative to creative, and grief exposed to another, you know where I am.

#3962. "We've finally reached this milestone": Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP kicks off open beta after around six years preparing for cybermayhem

"Let's see how the project handles real player traffic"

After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics."

"Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "New features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!"

According to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

For info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

#3961. Pokémon Champions Is Adding Four More Mega Evolutions In A New Update Next Week

24 newly added Pokémon will also be available for battle

Following the news of a Pokémon Champions balance patch update, The Pokémon Company has now revealed some new competitors are preparing to arrive in the free-to-play battle title.

On 2nd December 2026, Regulation Set M-D will see the arrival of Mega Heatran and Mega Tatsugiri. All up, there will be 24 newly added Pokémon available for battle and four more Mega Evolutions.

Here's the full announcement from the official Pokémon website:

Some new competitors are preparing for battle! Regulation Set M-D will run in Pokémon Champions from Wednesday, December 2, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. PST to Wednesday, March 3, 2027, at 5:59 p.m. PST. Pokémon that were eligible for Ranked Battles in previous regulation sets remain eligible, but they’ll be joined by Heatran, Dondozo, Tatsugiri, and more!

Even more Mega Evolutions are gearing up for a fight under Regulation Set M-D, including Mega Heatran and Mega Tatsugiri. Following the update, there will be a total of 24 newly added Pokémon available for battle, along with four Mega Evolutions.

You can see the full roster in your game by following these steps:

- Go to Recruit. - Select Recruit Pokémon. - Select Roster Info.

Best of luck with your battles in Pokémon Champions, Trainers!

Here's some more information about what you can expect from Mega Heatran and Mega Tatsugiri (via Serebii.net):

- Mega Heatran has Water Compaction, which boosts its Defense by 2 Stages when hit by a Water-type Move - Mega Tatsugiri has a new Ability which increases its Special Attack by 1 stage when it enters battle

Again, this will arrive alongside a balance update on the same date. You can find out more about this in last week's post.

#3959. The Rings of Power season 3 episode 7 director breaks down the "huge pressure" of forging the One Ring for the first time on screen

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Get the biggest gaming news, reviews, and releases straight to your inbox.

Bringing all the latest movie news, features, and reviews to your inbox

Unlock instant access to exclusive member features.

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

Exclusive: Imagining how Tolkien "might have created" the One Ring sequence was central

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Rings of Power season 3 has now aired its most dramatic moment yet: the forging of the One Ring. In episode 7, Sauron enters Mount Doom and gives everything he has to create the ultimate weapon in his quest for power in Middle-earth.

Creating the sequence was the culmination of years of work for The Rings of Power showrunners JD Payne and Patrick McKay, and for the episode's director, Stefan Schwartz, bringing it to screen for the first time came with "huge pressure".

"You've got so many massive Rings fans and it's tricky because there's nothing in any of the books that describe how the Ring was created, and we scoured everything to try and glean any little bits and pieces," he tells GamesRadar+. "So really approaching that scene, we had to create a whole bunch of new thoughts."

For Schwartz, a lot of this came down to making sure the sequence was magical, and really represented the world that Tolkien created. One element of that was imagining that the One Ring was created by the vibrations of Fëanor's hammer in Mount Doom, rather than simply being forged.

"I wanted Mount Doom to be a real character and actually to work with him rather than just be a place where he happens to be," he explains. "At [Middle-earth's] very inception, a song was created, and then a little bit of darkness was introduced by the song through one of the characters, and then this song created Middle-earth. That music felt really key, and Tom Bombadil is always singing, it seems key to Tolkien's world. So I wanted the idea of music and vibration to be in there."

Another interesting addition to the sequence is how Sauron ends up giving his life to creating the One Ring, before it brings him back. Schwartz said they wanted to play with the audience a bit here too. "The other key moment for all of us was sacrifice, that Sauron has to basically give up his life in order to create the ring, and then the ring brings back his life," he adds. "That moment of death and utter silence was really important."

The final sequence is undoubtedly the show's most cinematic moment yet, and it's little wonder they wanted to bring it to theaters for a special screening. However, beyond spectacle, it seems that, above all, those involved wanted to do justice to the world that Tolkien created.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

"When you've got such an avid fan base, you want to try and be as true as you can be to the lore," Schwartz sums it up. "And then work within that and try to get elements that feel intuitive and connected to if Tolkien had created it, what he might have created."

The Rings of Power season 3 is available to watch on Prime Video now. Check out out The Rings of Power season 3 review for our full verdict as well as everything you need to know about The Rings of Power season 4.

#3958. God of War Laufey Star Will Reprise Role for Live-Action TV Show

God of War Laufey’s lead Deborah Ann Woll will reprise her role as Kratos’ wife Faye in Amazon Prime’s upcoming live-action TV adaptation.

The actress – who also played the character in God of War Ragnarok – will star opposite Dave Bautista’s Kratos in the glitzy show.

The re-telling should end up feeling quite familiar, as Alastair Duncan will also return as Mimir.

Fans of the franchise will know Woll dies at the start of the story, kickstarting Kratos’ quest as he and son Atreus embark on a journey to scatter her ashes.

But we now know, during that period, Faye is trapped in a kind of afterlife for the gods known as the Everywhen. That’s where God of War Laufey will take place.

It’ll be interesting to see whether the TV show pulls in elements from the upcoming PS5 game, or if Woll’s role here will be to show Kratos’ family life prior to the events of the main game.

There’s no release date for the show just yet, but filming restarted in October with Baustita in the lead role, after previous actor Ryan Hurst was recast due to sustaining an injury on set.

Woll is an accomplished actress and knows the character inside-out, so this casting makes perfect sense to me.

#3957. "Nobody was hurt" in shooting near Clockwork Revolution devs InXile Entertainment's office, the Xbox-owned studio and police confirm

"Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is currently being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

"Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson said in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

"We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile said in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

InXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

Since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power."

Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

Xbox is bagging up former PlayStation exclusives like crazy, with Nioh 3 Complete Edition making its way to Xbox Series X|S on January 28, 2027.

Nioh follows Helldivers 2, the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy and PHYSINT by hopping aboard Xbox hardware. It's lovely to see renowned franchises like the dark samurai souls-like Nioh arrive on Xbox. It certainly beats seeing Halo and Gears launch on PS5 without anything major coming the other way.

Nioh 3 Complete Edition is an action RPG, in which players don the role of shogun Takechiyo, facing off against punishing soulslike scraps and challenges. Team NINJA shared a press release confirming the game is headed to Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox on January 28, 2027, complete with Xbox Play Anywhere support.

Nioh 3's second DLC, Bloody Insurrection, is set for December 17, 2026 for PS5 and Steam. The DLC will be included in the Complete Edition when it arrives early next year. As a franchise, Nioh has consistently wooed players with it's punishing combat and flashy action, with the third game holding an 86 on Metacritic.

Exciting times, eh? I wonder if this means Xbox players might gain access to Nioh 1 or 2 ports at some point in the future. Personally, I've always heard good things about the Nioh games, so it would be great to experience the entire series on Xbox, should Koei Tecmo make them available.

Takechiyo must traverse time to change their fate and rescue a Japan overridden with yokai. Explore rich open fields and switch between Samurai and Ninja Styles instantaneously in battle. Encounter figures from history, and experience the tense battles characteristic of the Nioh series.

#3955. The Witch Life-Sim Witchbrook Has Officially "Gone Gold"

During the Indie World Showcase in October, it was confirmed the witch-themed life-sim and social RPG Witchbrook would be coming to the Switch 1 & 2 on 28th January 2027.

In an update from the developer this week, the team has now reassured Nintendo fans it's locked in for this date, as the game has officially "gone gold" on all platforms. Here's the message, along with a fitting in-game screenshot:

"We're delighted to announce that Witchbrook has GONE GOLD ALL PLATFORMS! We're can't wait for you all to join us on the journey on Jan 28th!"

Again, this basically means everything is currently on schedule, and the master copy is ready to go. Of course, "going gold" in the digital age means teams can still spend time polishing their title before the launch.

In this particular case, Witchbrook is getting an eShop release (with a physical version to follow), and we can probably expect some patches and updates as well. It was recently confirmed Witchbrook would also support crossplay between Switch 1 & 2 on release.

#3954. The Rings of Power season 3 ending explained: who dies, what happens to Sauron, and more

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Everything you need to know about The Rings of Power season 3 ending

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Rings of Power season 3 ending is a surprising one, as the Dark Lord Sauron's last move of this installment is something you probably weren't expecting.

In episode 7, he finally forged the One Ring, which means his victory was seemingly at hand as Númenor and the Elves gathered to stop him. The main action of the episode, however, is reserved for Gandalf and the Blue Wizard Pallando. Below, we break down all the twists and turns of the episode, so you can get up to speed at a glance.

That means there are spoilers ahead, so turn back now if you're not up to date. For everything you need to know about The Rings of Power season 3 ending, head to the below.

The Rings of Power season 3 ending kicks off with the armies of Númenor and the Elves about to face Sauron's army of Orcs and men in battle. Sauron has the Blue Wizard Pallando on his side, and, of course, the Dark Lord just finished forging the infamous One Ring to Rule Them All.

Yet all is not smooth sailing for Sauron. Gandalf proves impossible to corrupt, even after Sauron tries to trick him with a vision of his old Harfoot pal Nori. Meanwhile, Galadriel introduces Celeborn to Elrond and Gil-galad, and Pharazôn decides to fight Sauron despite the terrifying size of the Dark Lord's army.

Sauron gifts Pallando a ring and makes a reference to the wizard becoming the Witch-king. However, it seems this is not Pallando's fate, as Gandalf is able to slip the ring from Pallando's finger and return his old friend to the light side. Sadly, Pallando is stabbed through the chest – though the wizard is able to survive long enough to help Gandalf get rid of Khamûl. Pallando's death spurs the men from Rhûn to abandon the fight.

Gandalf then encounters Tom Bombadil, who is not tempted by Pallando's ring at all. In fact, he takes it from Gandalf and makes it disappear, then declines Gandalf's offer of his hat. Classic Tom.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Finally, Theo warns Sauron that their forces are now evenly matched with the opposing side's, and Sauron reads a letter from Pharazôn gloating that Númenor is the "king of men." Bizarrely, Sauron chooses to surrender. While Pharazôn laughs heartily, relishing his victory, Gil-galad, Galadriel, and Elrond are more doubtful. The season ends with Sauron smirking, as his theme music plays ominously in the background.

There is only one significant death in The Rings of Power season 3 finale: Pallando. He is stabbed through the chest by a Nazgnagôl, but he dies redeemed. His death makes the forces of Rhûn abandon the incoming war, which turns the tide in favor of the Elves and Númenor. Also killed in this episode is Khamûl, the Nazgnagôl who snared Pallando to Sauron's side in the first place.

Sauron tells Pallando that he could become "a Witch-king no man can slay." Speculation has been rife about who might become the Witch-king in the show, and this seemed to answer all of those questions… until Pallando dies, anyway. The Witch-king is a dark figure, leader of the Ringwraiths, who is ultimately killed by Eowyn (as seen in The Return of the King). With Pallando ruled out, it once again looks like Theo is the likeliest candidate, especially since he couldn't resist rescuing his ring after Galadriel tried to destroy it in episode 7.

Nori returns thanks to a vision from Sauron, meant to deceive Gandalf into joining his side. However, Gandalf is able to figure out that he's not really seeing his old friend by referencing her brother. Then, the illusion ends. Later in the episode we catch a glimpse of the real Nori, looking up at the sky, as Gandalf brings Pallando back to the light. It seems she's not been taken by Sauron at all, and may return in the upcoming season 4.

Galadriel threw Theo's ring into a pot of molten metal to free him from its influence in episode 7. However, Theo was unable to walk away, still mesmerized by its power. So, we can assume he retrieved the ring and returned to Sauron's service in between episodes.

Tom Bombadil makes Pallando's ring disappear, which so impresses Gandalf he offers the other man his hat (which Tom gracefully declines). Just what he has actually done with the ring is unknown for now, since we know for a fact that Sauron will eventually have all nine rings in his power to give to his Ringwraiths.

Since the beginning of the series, there have been ominous signs that Númenor is doomed (as it is in Tolkien's source material). When Sauron surrenders, Pharazôn gloats, while Gil-galad says he sees the "doom of men" in the action. In Tolkien's works, Númenor is essentially destroyed as a punishment for hubris, when it invades the Undying Lands, AKA Valinor, to try and take immortality. Pharazôn is certainly showing this kind of doomed arrogance, which Sauron seems to be taking advantage of – indeed, in Tolkien, Sauron manipulates Pharazôn as his prisoner, and it looks like this storyline is coming in season 4, judging by that smirk.

Sauron receives a letter from Pharazôn gloating that Númenor is the "king of men." It seems the Dark Lord sees some opportunity here, as he immediately goes to surrender to the forces of Númenor and the Elves. While the Elves are wary, Pharazôn is delighted. However, in Tolkien's works, Sauron helps bring about the end of Númenor by manipulating Pharazôn as his prisoner. It looks like this is Sauron's next scheme, signalled by his devious smirk.

Before surrendering, Sauron takes off the One Ring. However, he has most likely concealed it somewhere he can wear it again when he needs it, since we know from Tolkien's work this is not the end of the Dark Lord.

Yes, Amazon has officially announced that there will be a The Rings of Power season 4. The series is in pre-production now and will begin filming in the UK in spring.

No, there is no Rings of Power season 3 post-credits scene. Once the episode ends, you're free to turn it off.

All episodes of The Rings of Power season 3 are streaming on Prime Video now. For more, check out our The Rings of Power season 3 review.

#3951. GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty to 2022 Rockstar Games breach which the company claim cost them $5 million

Hacker was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital

A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

The BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

Kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the company contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two quickly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely shows anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

Black Friday Nintendo Switch 2 deals are hitting the shelves this week, with Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, GameStop and Target all launching official sales and Ninty itself dropping the holiday bundle of the year. The heavy hitter here is the Mario Kart World package, shedding $50 from its $549.99 MSRP to land at the same $499 price as the handheld by itself - only with a free copy of the game and three months of Nintendo Switch Online Individual included as well.

Already got a handheld? That's where Black Friday Nintendo Switch 2 game deals come in handy. A range of titles are $20 off officially right now, giving us the first major discount on Donkey Kong Bananza as well as a chunky reduction on games like Kirby Air Riders and Super Mario Party Jamboree.

Those first party Black Friday Switch deals are still all holding their position on the shelves (impressive considering I've seen bundles selling out the weekend before the main event in years gone by), but third party accessories and games are also getting involved. We've been hands-on with all the latest and greatest gadgets for the entire Switch 2 and OG Switch lifespan, so we're bringing you the biggest discounts on the tech we recommend every day right here.

We've still got a couple of days to go before Black Friday proper, but there's already plenty to sink your teeth into before the turkey's even served. You'll find our top picks below, but we're live tracking price drops and stock levels throughout the whole event further down the page as well.

I've been tracking Black Friday Nintendo Switch deals for over seven years now, starting as a dedicated Deals Editor at our sister site TechRadar. That's where I learned how to spot value on the shelves, and price track to find the deals that are actually worth your time. In my time at GamesRadar+ I've been hands-on with the latest and greatest Switch and Switch 2 accessories. That means I know the gadgets you should be prioritizing and how much you should pay for them.

A range of retailers have the Mario Kart World Switch 2 bundle live on the shelves this Black Friday, but Amazon is shedding an extra 99 cents off that final price. This is Nintendo's headliner this year, with a free copy of the latest kart racer and three months of Switch Online.

Donkey Kong Bananza launched not long after the Switch 2 itself, but it's been stuck at full price since then. Today's Black Friday price marks its first major saving on that $69.99 MSRP and its lowest price ever by some way.

However, with a free copy of Mario Kart World (worth $79.99) and three months of NSO Individual (worth $7.99) up for grabs elsewhere, value isn't on Woot's side right now. The equation is this, would you rather save $30 and buy a cheaper game or get $87.98 worth of value in freebies?

With no discounts on the official Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller in sight, it's worth weighing up whether that $89 price tag is worth it after all.

Here's what the Nintendo does that others... Nintendon't.

The Switch 2 Pro Controller is unmatched in its ability to wake the Switch 2. Others can, and will, bring that screen to life in docked mode, but setup is finnicky and dropouts are regular. The Switch 2 talks to its own gamepad best.

You also won't find Nintendo-specific HD Rumble 2 haptics in third party alternatives. That's the more nuanced level of vibration that makes games like Donkey Kong Bananza sing just that little bit brighter. Haptics are available in third parties, but without that Ninty spark.

Finally, onscreen control over your back button assignments is exclusive to Nintendo's gamepad. Being able to quickly pause your game and configure each of the two additional clickers is super handy - others will have you connecting to a PC or mobile app, or working out individual button presses on the gamepad itself.

If any of those are deal breakers, the Switch 2 Pro Controller is worth it. If you can live without those luxuries, though, third parties have plenty to bring to the table. GameSir and 8BitDo add trigger stops, Hall effect thumbsticks, charging docks, and extra configurable buttons to the party, for example.

The Genki Covert Dock 3 is the latest in a long line of pocket-friendly Switch docks that look just like regular power adapters. Otherwise I'd be using my right thumb to hold down that tiny button while losing all camera controls at the same time. It makes my cinematic sweeps across Hyrule impossible, and means I can't check my 6 for that oncoming ReDead.

I played the campaign in docked mode, squished right up against the TV to check out those Fairy Fountains in 4K. If you're taking on this adventure in handheld mode, I can't recommend a Joy-Con alternative with back buttons enough.

The CRKD Nitro Deck 2 has won this battle. With four clackers to the rear and a chunky set of ergonomically-minded grips, it's become our default for adding features and comfort to the Switch 2 handheld experience. It's pricey, though, far pricier than the previous generation.

TMR thumbsticks replace the Hall effect installation on GameSir's cheaper pad, adding an extra level of precision and control across those asymmetric toppers. The rest is pretty similar, with a charging dock in the box, plenty of customization options, and split Switch and PC compatibility.

The Switch 2 Pro Controller is one of the more expensive first-party gamepads in PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo's little race. That Pro Controller price is a lot more flexible in the UK, spending far more time at £59.99 than it does the full £75. Considering that new rate has become a mainstay on UK shelves, we could see retailers kicking things down to around £55.

Over in the US, Pro Controller price cuts are proving incredibly difficult to chance upon. That launch price has remained stubborn ever since last year. The SteelSeries Arctis Nova 3 Wireless mentioned earlier sits at the bottom of its brand's lineup. Closer to the top end sits the best set of cups we've ever tested; the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni.

Hear me now, though. The Omni is only worth the upgrade if you play across multiple platforms. Those with a Switch 2, PC, and PS5 or Xbox Series X all in one setup are going to feel the benefit of that much higher $399.99 MSRP a lot quicker. The hot-swappable batteries, boost in audio processing, and easy EQ customization makes sense for those after a real investment headset. That could be a sign that things are happening behind the scenes, though, so I'd keep this one firmly on your radar.

The Razer Barracuda X has been doing the rounds for some time now, but as a low-cost wireless headset that still manages to impress in its versatility and power it should do. This is an older release, and it generally only ever drops to today's $68.99 sale price during day to day offers - but anyone on the hunt for something a little more premium than Turtle Beach's outing should be taking note.

It's generally a toss-up between this and the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 3 for Switch 2 value. Both are at similar prices right now (SteelSeries' venture is down to $69.99 at Amazon), so which should you go for?

In my experience, the Arctis Nova 3X is going to offer a slightly wider range of audio. It's got a wider soundstage and a minor boost in texture and richness compared to the older set. However, Razer's still my top recommendation when both are the same price.

It's got 10 hours more battery life, spatial audio baked in with virtual surround sound, and more subtle design that translates better for everyday listening.

Razer Barracuda X | $99.99 $68.99 at Best Buy

The GameSir Super Nova is back on sale for $29.99 at Best Buy (was $49.99) after dropping out of stock earlier in the week. That's a record-low position it frequently returns to during major sales events. It's also a discount that stands in the way of a number of slightly more expensive gamepads, so I knew I had to get it in my own hands before Black Friday.

What do you get for your money? Quite a lot.

The Super Nova feels far more premium than that $30 price tag would suggest. While alternatives like the PowerA Advantage Wired Controller can undercut it by around $10 when the discounts are flowing, they also feel light, hollow, and creaky in the hands. This is as solid as it gets, with nicely rubberized grips, satisfying buttons, and a premium heft.

Customization is your main point of value in this price. Back buttons are par for the course these days, and trigger-stops are creeping down the price scale as well, but motion controls can also be mapped to mouse inputs on PC, GameSir's Connect software can change everything from stick deadzones to trajectory settings, and - of course - that RGB is configurable as well.

Is it perfect? No. I scored the GameSir Super Nova 4/5 stars in my review, dropping points for its lack of presets, rigid-feeling d-pad, and finnicky wake functionality. The latter is a particularly sore point. It was one of the biggest reasons I was so excited to wrap my hands around this gamepad, but in all my testing I just never got it to work. It's a fairly convoluted setup process anyway, but others have been able to get everything running smoothly.

Ultimately, paying more for the GameSir Super Nova over budget gamepads from PowerA and PDP is a no-brainer in my experience.

GameSir Super Nova | $49.99 $29.99 at Best Buy

I know, Mario Party Jamboree is fun with friends and there's history in Super Mario Galaxy 1 & 2, but if we're going on value alone, Donkey Kong Bananza has to be up at the top of my personal Switch 2 game recommendation list this week.

While it's not going to give SteelSeries, Razer, or Corsair anything to worry about, we were still impressed with the power and detailing in this sound at a $30 price point.

It ticked all the right boxes in testing; slick design, comfortable form factor, easy connection, and a value-packed price point. Those after fancier features will still be left wanting here, but anyone after a quick and easy upgrade over the system's speakers will be happy here.

The PowerA Slim Case isn't a particularly flashy recommendation, but it is a damn good clamshell at its lowest price yet this Black Friday. #3948. Intel are being sued for "misleading" investors about "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory" thanks to AI-fuelled price hikes

Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.

All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they announced a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

The lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation". In a press release, they say they've filed suit on behalf of anybody who bought Intel stock from July 23rd to October 29th this year.

The suit claims that Intel neglected to tell investors that falling PC and component sales were having a "materially greater negative impact" on their third financial quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Groupresults than Intel had previously stated – to the tune of "hundreds of millions of dollars" in revenue shrinkage, compared to the previous quarter, with the situation still expected to "worsen".

They also accuse the company of keeping schtum about the aforesaid "massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", together with the fact that "any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described above."

Finally, they say Intel bosses have failed to disclose that they're struggling to procure an adequate supply of substrates – that is, materials used to create the base layer of chips, circuit boards and similar components. As such, the lawyers claim, Intel couldn't "ramp up production to meet data center CPU demand even if the Company chose to divert production resources because of a slowdown in PC-related sales."

Once the Godzilla of personal computing, Intel haven't been having a brilliant few years. Back in 2024, they recorded a multi-billion dollar quarterly loss, pushing then-CEO Pat Gelsinger to resign. As regards sales of gaming PCs, they've fallen behind AMD, though they've reportedly taken some ground back recently as regards desktop CPUs. As regards graphics cards, they have long been dwarfed by Nvidia.

Any Intel investor who wants a piece of that lawsuit has until January 12th 2027 to sign up as a lead plaintiff – that is, a court appointee who represents the interests of other class members. As regards us little people who don't buy stock in huge technology corporations, all this merely continues the weird existential crisis wrought upon 'traditional' gaming and computing hardware by the feckless quest to sell a better chatbot.

#3947. Today Is Your Last Chance to Play Destruction AllStars on PS5

Forgotten car combat game Destruction AllStars has been in some stage of extinction for years now, but if you do have the PS5 game in your library, then today truly is the last day you can play it in any meaningful manner.

From tomorrow, 25th November 2026, the last of its game services will be taken offline.

The multiplayer servers were already permanently pulled in May 2026, and within the next 24 hours, "all remaining game services will be taken offline", per communication from Sony.

Single player modes had still been available to play, but those will be removed too when their servers are taken offline.

Quite literally the only content left in Destruction AllStars after tomorrow is an arcade mode and challenges. Even then, though, Sony warns the "functionality and player experience" tied to that content could be impacted.

Basically, if you want to experience even a sliver of the Destruction AllStars experience, you've only got today left to do it. It's already been delisted from the PS Store, so if you don't have a copy now, you're completely out of luck.

It's not like you'd be missing out on much, to be fair.

Destruction AllStars never made a splash in terms of quality or popularity. While it did have a small playerbase during its days with active servers, the game quickly died out after a February 2021 release.

Will you be playing Destruction AllStars one last time today? Let us know in the comments below.

#3946. Lords Of The Fallen 2 Launches April 2027, Final Date Coming Next Month

Publisher CI Games has announced that Lords of the Fallen 2 will launch in April 2027.

This comes via a social media post from founder and CEO Marek Tyminski (thanks, Gematsu), who simply said "Lords of the Fallen II: April 2027. Exact date in December". So yes, we'll keep an eye out for a further update and let you know when exactly you can expect the game to drop.

The game was previously delayed into 'Q1 2027' earlier this year, with Tyminski explaining that the stacked 2026 schedule – which includes Zelda: Ocarina of Time and a little game called GTA 6 – led to a desire to give Lords of the Fallen 2 a bit of space to shine.

"This updated release window also strategically positions Lords of the Fallen II outside of a highly competitive holiday period, ensuring the game receives the dedicated attention it deserves."

It's honestly not a bad choice at all, and we're thankful to see at least one game escape the avalanche of releases in 2026. Hell, we've still got a bunch of big-hitters coming in December, including Rayman Legends Retold, Monster Hunter Wilds, Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World, and Professor Layton and The New World of Steam.

#3945. GTA 6's Most Spectacular Easter Egg So Far Has Just Been Discovered

Update [Tue 24th Nov 2026, 2:27pm]: Our sister site Push Square has also now published a guide for this Easter Egg:

Guide GTA 6: Vice City Easter Egg Walkthrough & Tommy Vercetti Shirt Unlock

Push SquareFind the portal and get your Tommy Vercetti rewards

Original Story: One of the coolest things about GTA 6 since release has been watching players discover all kinds of Easter Eggs, such as the Mario-inspired hats that were shared by our sister site Nintendo Life yesterday.

We reckon this is the best one so far though - a secret portal that takes you into a nightclub from the original 2002 version of Vice City for the PS2 (which technically means it takes you back to its 1986-inspired setting).

The process of getting here is long-winded, and detailed in full in the video from Dan Allen Gaming up above. In a nutshell, you have to go to the Badger R&D Radio Tower in Key Lento and use the power switch and press a button to make the Malibu logo appear on the TV. From there, visit 12 LPL substations around the map without fast-travelling, and press the correct buttons in the specific order (from the video) when you reach them. You'll then get a text, at which point you head to Reactor 2 at the LPL Turtle Head Power Station between 7pm and 6am to find the portal.

It seems someone called Memelo was the first to discover this trick:

Another really cool part of this Easter Egg is that when you combine all the substations together, the wording on the outside of them adds up to "Life is Passing Me By", which references a classic cheat code from the original Vice City. You actually have to use the buttons to enter this cheat code and make the portal appear.

As mentioned, you get two free items for your trouble as well, which are Tommy Vercetti's classic shirt and bike from the 2002 game. These appear as soon as you're thrown out of the portal and back into the so-called real world!

Finally, we'll also highlight that although pretty much all the footage we've seen of this Easter Egg has been exclusive to the Jason character, it does appear to work with Lucia as well. That said, we've also come across many players who claim the portal isn't showing up for them, so we're not sure what's causing it to fail in those situations.

Anyway, crazy stuff right?! Who knows what other insane Easter Eggs might be discovered over the coming days and weeks - some people have mentioned they're seeing a "flashback" pop-up after completing the Vice City one, with a suggestion there may be another four flashback sequences yet to be found. Let's hope so!
